sentences.text: In the case on hand the plaintiff approached the court with specific case that he is absolute owner in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property by virtue of the registered gift deed executed by his wife on 08.08.2014.
Earlier to that his wife purchased the said property from Rasheed Pasha who is the GPA holder of C.Ramu and C.Lingaraju who are children of R.Channappa.
Earlier the suit property was belongs to R.Channappa and he purchased the said property under registered sale deed dated 26.06.1939.
After the death of said R.Channappa his sons C.Ramu and C.Lingaraju have formed layout and sold sites to different persons.
However as there was bar for execution of registered sale deed they executed GPA in favour of Mr.Rasheed Pasha S/o Noor Pasha.
The defendant is neither owner nor in possession of suit schedule property.
However the officials of defendant tried to interfere with his possession on 05.01.2019 and they tried to demolish the suit schedule property.
26. As admitted by plaintiff the suit schedule property is situated in Sy.No.174 & 175 of Kacharakanahalli Vaillage.
According to plaintiff the said property was belongs to R.Channappa.
The said R.Channappa was having sons by name C.Ramu and C.Lingaraju.
As could be seen from Ex.D2 the O.S. No.25531/2019 award was passed in view of the acquisition of Sy.No.174.
In the said award it is also mentioned in page No.2 that C.Lingaraju and C.Ramu legal heirs of Channappa have given claim to the office of defendant and on 08.04.1986 the award was passed.
Hence, the land in Sy.No.174 & 175 of Kacharakanahalli Village are already been acquired by the defendant authority under the BDA Act.
27. According to defendant on acquiring the said property the possession was also taken and the plaintiff has no right to challenge the acquisition proceedings or the possession of the property.

Under the circumstances the defendant is denying not only the possession of plaintiff but also the very title of the plaintiff and have specifically contended that the suit schedule property is vested with defendant and hence the suit is not maintainable.
Hence the very title of the plaintiff is under challenge.
The plaintiff no where in the plaint pleaded regarding the acquisition of Sy.No.174 & 175 of Kacharakanahalli Village.
However the documents relied on by the defendant goes to show that Sy.No.174 & 175 of Kacharakanahalli Village was acquired by the BDA under BDA Act.
The suit schedule property as amditted by PW.1 in his cross-examination is situated in Sy.No.174 & 175 of Kacharakanahalli Village only.
When that being the case there is a cloud over the title of the plaintiff over the suit schedule property.

In this regard this court intends to rely on the Judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Anathula Sudhakar Vs. P. Buchi Redddy (Dead) by LR's and Others reported in AIR 2008 SC 2033 wherein it is held as follows:

sentences.text: Where the title of plaintiff is under a cloud or in dispute and he is not in possession or not able to O.S. No.25531/2019 establish possession, necessarily the plaintiff will have to file a suit for declaration, possession and injunction.

12. We may however clarify that a prayer for declaration will be necessary only if the denial of title by the defendant or challenge to plaintiff's title raises a cloud on the title of plaintiff to the property.
A cloud is said to raise over a person's title, when some apparent defect in his title to a property, or when some prima facie right of a third party over it, is made out or shown.

An action for declaration,
is the remedy to remove the cloud on the title to the property.

On the other hand, where the plaintiff has clear title supported by documents, if a trespasser without any claim to title or an interloper without any apparent title, merely denies the plaintiff's title, it does not amount to raising a cloud over the title of the plaintiff and it will not be necessary for the plaintiff to sue for declaration and a suit for injunction may be sufficient.

Where the plaintiff, believing that defendant is only a trespasser or a wrongful claimant without title, files a mere suit for injunction, and in such a suit,
the defendant discloses in his defence the details of the right or title claimed by him, which raises a serious dispute or cloud over plaintiff's title, then there is a need for the plaintiff, to amend the plaint and convert the suit into one for declaration.
Alternatively, he may withdraw the suit for bare injunction, with permission of the court to file a comprehensive suit for declaration and injunction.

He may file the suit for declaration with consequential relief, even after the suit for injunction is dismissed, where the suit raised only the issue of possession and not any issue of title.
29.

In the case on hand the defendant has specifically contended that plaintiff is not owner nor title holder of the suit schedule property as the suit schedule property is already O.S. No.25531/2019 acquired by the defendant and as the defendant authority is in lawful possession of the suit schedule property.
When that being the case the plaintiff has to seek the relief of declaration and mere suit for permanent injunction is not maintainable.

sentences.text: I have gone through the decisions relied on by the plaintiff and defendant.
As discussed above the very title of O.S. No.25531/2019
the plaintiff in respect of suit schedule property which is carved out of Sy.No.174 & 175 of Kacharakanahalli Village is itself is in dispute.

The defendant authority is claiming the suit schedule property on the ground that the same was acquired vide final notification on 09.01.1985 itself and it is the defendant authority which is in lawful possession of suit schedule property.

33. The vendors of plaintiff's wife i.e., C.Ramu and C.Lingaraju have also appeared before defendant authority as LR's of late R.Channappa and their presence is shown in Ex.D2 at page No.2 and award is already passed as per Ex.D2.
Under the circumstances the vendors of the plaintiff's wife themselves had no absolute title to convey the suit property to the wife of plaintiff.
Under the circumstances, the argument of the plaintiff that he is in lawful possession of suit schedule property cannot be accepted.
The plaintiff has to seek the O.S. No.25531/2019 relief of declaration of his title.

The plaintiff though contended that the officials of defendant came near the suit property on 05.01.2019 and they tried to interfere with his possession is also not established by any cogent and convincing evidence.
Hence, mere suit for permanent injunction filed by plaintiff is not maintainable and the plaintiff has to seek the relief of declaration of his title to the suit schedule property.
Accordingly, issue No.1 and 2 are answered in the negative and issue No.4 is answered in affirmative.

34. Issue No.3:
In view of my findings on issue No.1 & 2 in the negative the plaintiff is not entitled for the suit relief as prayed for.
Accordingly, I answered issued No.3 in the negative.
Issue No.5:

In view of the reasoning given above, I proceed to pass the following:-
O R D E R
The suit filed by the plaintiff as against the defendants is hereby dismissed with costs.
Draw decree accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The plaintiff has paid tax to the suit schedule property.
Now the plaintiff is running Saba Welfare Trust in the suit schedule property for the physically disabled children.
Accordingly, the plaintiff as well as his vendor wherein lawful possession and enjoyment the suit schedule property since several decades.
The plaintiff is also in settled possession and he cannot be dispossessed of the same without due process of law.
The defendant has no right over the suit schedule property.
Accordingly, the plaintiff has filed this suit and prays to decree the suit.

opennyai_summary.issue:
O.S. No.25531/2019 11. Based on the pleadings, my Predecessor-in-office has framed following:
I S S U E S 1) Whether plaintiff proves that he was in lawful possession and enjoying the suit property at the time of filing of the suit?
2) Whether the plaintiff proves that the defendant had interfered with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property?
3) Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the relief sought in the plaint?
4) Whether the defendant proves that suit is not maintainable?
5) What order or decree?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Subsequently the wife of the plaintiff gifted the said property to the plaintiff through registered gift deed dated 08.08.2014.
Since the date of gift O.S. No.25531/2019 deed the plaintiff is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property.
18. On the contrary it is the specific defence of the defendant that the suit is not maintainable.
The plaintiff has suppressed the material facts.
Any GPA or sale deed or encumbrance subsequent to the said notification does not bind the defendant.
The subsequent purchaser has no right to challenge the legality of the acquisition proceedings.
The plaintiff or his wife are not in possession of the suit schedule property.
Hence, the land in Sy.No.174 & 175 of Kacharakanahalli Village are already been acquired by the defendant authority under the BDA Act.
27. According to defendant on acquiring the said property the possession was also taken and the plaintiff has no right to challenge the acquisition proceedings or the possession of the property.
Under the circumstances the defendant is denying not only the possession of plaintiff but also the very title of the plaintiff and have specifically contended that the suit schedule property is vested with defendant and hence the suit is not maintainable.
When that being the case there is a cloud over the title of the plaintiff over the suit schedule property.
On the other hand, where the plaintiff has clear title supported by documents, if a trespasser without any claim to title or an interloper without any apparent title, merely denies the plaintiff's title, it does not amount to raising a cloud over the title of the plaintiff and it will not be necessary for the plaintiff to sue for declaration and a suit for injunction may be sufficient.
When that being the case the plaintiff has to seek the relief of declaration and mere suit for permanent injunction is not maintainable.
The defendant authority is claiming the suit schedule property on the ground that the same was acquired vide final notification on 09.01.1985 itself and it is the defendant authority which is in lawful possession of suit schedule property.
Under the circumstances the vendors of the plaintiff's wife themselves had no absolute title to convey the suit property to the wife of plaintiff.
The plaintiff has to seek the O.S. No.25531/2019 relief of declaration of his title.
The plaintiff though contended that the officials of defendant came near the suit property on 05.01.2019 and they tried to interfere with his possession is also not established by any cogent and convincing evidence.
Hence, mere suit for permanent injunction filed by plaintiff is not maintainable and the plaintiff has to seek the relief of declaration of his title to the suit schedule property.
